summary: Keisuke Fujii is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1986, earning a doctorate in engineering) and held posts there from 1982 to 2018, as well as at Tokyo University of the Arts.

Keith Dowman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1986) and held positions at Shuchiin University (~1993–2008) and Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2017).

Kelsang Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ngamring Chöde, Chambaling, Tashi Lhunpo, and Sera monasteries, and under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

Kelsey Alise Seymour works in Sinology and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018) and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
Kemo Jin was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and Peking University, where he became Professor of Sanskrit in 1948.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. from the University of British Columbia (~1968–1970) and studied under Kalu Rinpoche and other teachers. He was resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985–1990) and founded Unfettered Mind.

Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Florida (2008–2015), studying under Mario Poceski. He held assistant professorships at Young Harris College (2014–2018) and the University of Georgia (2018).

Kendall Wayne Folkert worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Western Michigan University, the University of Göttingen under Carsten Colpe, and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Central Michigan University (~1974–1985).

Kengo Harimoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees at Nagasaki University and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD under Wilhelm Halbfass). He has held posts at institutions including Mahidol University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

Kenichi Kuranishi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions as an associate professor at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii is a scholar of religious studies. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1983) and held a post at Kokugakuin University around 1989.
Kenji Kinugawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1979) under teachers including Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Kenji Matsuo works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and held a post at Yamagata University (~1989–2020).
Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941) and later worked there as a researcher (~1953–1981).

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi, as well as an exchange at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He was a JSPS-sponsored fellow at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).
Kenji Watanabe specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jozef Deleu and held a post as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1978–1980).
Kenjiu Kasawara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford from 1879, where his teachers included Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University (~1913–1916) and under Kitaro Nishida (~1922–1925). He held a post at Hirosaki University (~1949–1953).

Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1924–1947), where he became professor emeritus, and at Kurume University (~1950–1963).
